channel.title: Kathamndu post RSS
channel.description: The Kathmandu Post : Find the latest breaking news from Nepal, opinion and analysis on Nepali politics, business, culture and arts, sports, movies, food and travel, books, education, auto and more at kathmandupost.com

item.title: Bagmati chief minister set to resign ahead of floor test
item.description: Indra Bahadur Baniya is expected to step down after addressing the provincial assembly, clearing the way for the UML and NCP to form a new coalition government.

item.title: Snake images adorn homes as devotees mark Nag Panchami
item.description: Hindu families across the country placed images of serpent deities above their doors and offered prayers, milk, flowers and other ritual items on the festival.

item.title: Q&A: I have spent most of my adult life in America, but my internal identification remains firmly Nepali.
item.description: Acclaimed author Samrat Upadhyay on his creative roots, decades of writing across continents, shifting landscape of Kathmandu and the enduring resilience of the Nepali psyche.

item.title: Trump orders Pentagon to cut back military exercises with South Korea
item.description: Trump’s move to scale back the annual Ulchi Freedom Shield drills comes as he seeks to revive diplomacy with North Korea, while Seoul faces growing pressure over its security role and refusal to join US-led actions against Iran.

item.title: At Re-Kriti, the product is the hero
item.description: The organisation turns discarded denim into bags and accessories, while asking consumers to reconsider what they buy, what they throw away, and what waste can become.

item.title: New Kathmandu festival brings Tarkovsky, Kapadia and Nepali cinema together
item.description: The five-day ‘Licchavi Cinema Festival’ will bring films from Nepal, Asia, and beyond to Kathmandu, pairing contemporary works with classics.

item.title: Nepal revives industrial security force to restore investor confidence
item.description: The decision comes amid repeated incidents of vandalism and property damage as the government seeks to reassure the private sector and attract fresh investment.

item.title: Shusmita Thapa Magar begins her pro MMA journey with win
item.description: Magar has a pro Muay Thai record of 7-0 and a pro kickboxing record of 2-2. Now, she has entered MMA.

item.title: Commercial banks post 32 percent profit surge despite weak credit demand
item.description: Banks earned Rs69.78 billion in the last fiscal year, ended mid-July, as improved loan recoveries and lower provisioning lifted profits.

item.title: Landslides pile on the misery in Jajarkot settlements
item.description: The disasters highlight an escalating crisis across Jajarkot, where extreme weather is battering fragile communities still reeling from the earthquake.

item.title: Deuba faction’s Hindu line opens new fault line in Nepali Congress
item.description: A last-minute five-point declaration promotes Sanatan religion as a national identity, departing from an earlier 20-point conclusion and exposing divisions within the faction.

item.title: Monsoon disasters demand more than rescue
item.description: The government must identify where the risks lie before more disasters and deaths expose them.

item.title: The overlooked impact of inadequate rainfall and fertiliser shortages in Nepal’s agriculture sector
item.description: As long as the state undermines farmers’ plight, it cannot claim to act in the true interests of citizens.

item.title: Indian Army chief Dhiraj Seth arrives in Kathmandu for four-day visit
item.description: Seth is scheduled to receive the honorary rank of General of the Nepali Army from President Ramchandra Paudel on Monday and hold meetings with senior Nepali officials.

item.title: Death toll from Jajarkot landslide rises to four
item.description: A 70-year-old man who had been missing since Saturday evening was found buried about 50 metres below his home.

item.title: Five nominees unveiled for NSJF Pulsar Sports Award
item.description: NSJF eliminates paid voting to ensure a fairer contest for the 23rd Pulsar Sports Award’s People’s Choice category.

item.title: Minister Lamsal to return to Kathmandu after falling ill in Baitadi
item.description: The physical infrastructure development minister developed symptoms of a viral infection and common cold while on a tour of far-western districts.

item.title: Twelve killed and at least 10 injured in Polish bus crash in Hungary
item.description: State news agency MTI ​said there were 57 passengers and two drivers on the bus.

item.title: Non-resident Nepalis keen on domestic ventures, but cite bureaucratic hurdles and safety fears
item.description: Delegates at the 11th Asia-Pacific Regional Conference in Guangzhou urge the government to streamline legal procedures, improve security and lower interest rates to boost investment.

item.title: Nepal’s faith is finding a new interface
item.description: From horoscope apps and digital puja guides to robotic monks and chanting boxes, a small group of Nepali developers is testing whether technology can turn ancient religious practices into modern services.

item.title: In Karnali, basic healthcare can mean hours of waiting
item.description: Vacant specialist posts, overstretched doctors and inadequate equipment are leaving district hospitals unable to meet growing demand, forcing patients to travel elsewhere for treatment.

item.title: Three dead as landslides sweep houses in Rolpa and Jajarkot
item.description: One person remains missing as rescue teams struggle to reach areas cut off by blocked roads and repeated landslides.

item.title: Hopes fade in Colombia as more bodies recovered days after powerful quake
item.description: With rescue teams still searching unstable rubble for survivors, Colombia faces a growing humanitarian crisis as thousands remain displaced, hundreds are missing and authorities turn to body recovery and reconstruction.

item.title: When the snake call comes, Sagar Pandey answers
item.description: For 18 years, the 31-year-old self-taught expert from Palpa has rescued over 10,000 snakes—including a record 107 king cobras—across western Nepal, turning childhood fascination into a lifelong mission to protect wildlife.

item.title: At least 47 dead in eastern Indonesia after magnitude 7.7 quake
item.description: Rescuers struggle to reach the area closest to the epicentre as landslides block roads and disrupt communications, while aftershocks, damaged buildings and power outages hamper relief efforts.

item.title: Your skin needs a Nepal-specific routine for its climate, altitude and pollution
item.description: From Kathmandu’s pollution to the Tarai’s humidity and the mountains’ harsh UV exposure, dermatologist Shreya Bastakoti explains how to care for your skin according to where you live.

item.title: Fiction: So, you want to be a leader?
item.description: When everyone around you thinks you can save the country, it becomes difficult not to believe them.

item.title: How Youssef Wehbe and Soma Fight Club are pushing Rabindra Dhant and Yuki Angdembe to the pinnacle of MMA
item.description: Soma Fight Club’s head MMA coach Wehbe opens up about cornering and training Dhant and Angdembe, the power of Nepali fans, Gorkhali mentality, and why the country must invest in combat sports.

item.title: Non-domestic goods dominate Nepal’s exports as high-value products struggle
item.description: Exports of goods identified under the Nepal Trade Integrated Strategy grew just 3.16 percent last fiscal year, as weak domestic production, policy instability and poor coordination hamper efforts to diversify exports.

item.title: Subsidised rice reaches Humla through Chinese route after 7-year gap
item.description: Twenty-eight trucks carried the rice from Kathmandu to Kerung, where it was transferred into eight Chinese containers, each carrying 400 quintals, to Hilsa.

item.title: Government to allow NRN joint ventures to issue foreign-currency IPOs
item.description: Regulatory changes will allow a joint venture between the government and non-resident Nepalis to raise up to 85 percent of its capital from overseas investors.

item.title: Several settlements in Rolpa and Bajura at high risk of landslides, families face imminent displacement
item.description: Official inspection teams have concluded that some settlements need to be relocated.

item.title: Why Nepal’s economy will need more than a two-thirds majority
item.description: Four months in, the new government is discovering that good intentions don’t fix decades-old structural problems.

item.title: Nepal’s labour market caught between jobless workers and worker shortages
item.description: Weak skills recognition, poor job information and low wages are widening the gap between Nepal’s workers and employers.

item.title: How Nepal manages unidentified and unclaimed bodies
item.description: Police follow a set procedure to identify and trace relatives, but limited mortuary space means hospitals cannot preserve remains for long.

item.title: Indian Army chief Seth arriving Sunday amid uncertainty over meeting with PM Shah
item.description: General Dhiraj Seth will receive the honorary rank of General of the Nepali Army from the President on Monday.

item.title: India’s 80th Independence Day marked in Kathmandu
item.description: Indian embassy honours families of 11 deceased armed forces personnel and announces book grants for 22 educational institutions and libraries in Nepal.

item.title: NOC faces backlash over ID requirement for LPG buyers
item.description: The state oil monopoly says requiring citizenship certificates or National IDs is an initial trial to prevent hoarding during shortages.

item.title: Dengue cases surge to 289 in Baglung within a month
item.description: Health officials urge caution as the single-month tally surpasses the total recorded throughout the previous fiscal year.

item.title: Taliban mark five years in power as aid groups warn of crisis
item.description: Outside the former US embassy in Kabul, armoured Taliban vehicles took part in a parade, ‌displaying flags and banners, and celebrating what the government described as “victory day” from Western domination.
